end.summary:
- Sequenced Company’s rise from chartered trader to Crown rule, including Plassey, Buxar, Diwani and 1857.
- Explained forts, armies, alliances and battles as methods of gaining power.
- Explained the economic impact of British manufactured cloth on Indian weavers.
- Defined Diwani as the right to collect revenue and linked it to political control.
- Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Zoya practised how the East India Company expanded from trade to political rule. They used the sequence of the charter, Plassey, Buxar, Diwani and the 1857 revolt, and explained how revenue supported further control. They also connected imported British cloth with the decline of Indian weavers’ work. At home, ask Zoya to retell the sequence using five event cards and explain one effect of Diwani.
